predecessors.name: Pinya Kingdom
predecessors.text: "the northern province of Sagaing of the Pinya kingdom", which "claimed all the way to the border of Manipur"

successors.name: Kingdom of Ava
successors.text: "In 1365, Thado Minbya founded the kingdom of Ava and declared Sagaing and Pinya constituent countries of Ava"

ledger.x: 1315: Prince Saw Yun walks out of the Pinya Palace and founds the kingdom of Sagaing.
1315: the war of autonomy with Pinya begins.
1365: Thado Minbya founds the kingdom of Ava.

wars.name: Saw Yun's war of autonomy (Sagaing)
wars.outcome: Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy from his father King Thihathu in 1315-17"; formal secession in 1325.

wars.name: Sagaing-Pinya hostilities and the 1351 truce
wars.outcome: Shwetaungtet's expedition of 1339 to Mindon, "inside Pinya territory", brought Saw Yun's children back to Sagaing; "the situation turned cold again in 1340"; Princess Soe Min was sent in the 1350s to seek a truce with Kyawswa II, and the Pinya page has a…

wars.name: Maw Shan raids on Sagaing and Pinya
wars.outcome: "Maw troops also breached northern Sagaing territory in 1342 but they were driven back"; raids in 1356-57, 1358-59 and 1362-63 "overran the entire Sagaing countryside"; "In April 1364, Maw forces broke through, and entered the city" and the Maw sacked Pinya…

wars.name: Thado Minbya's conquest of Pinya
wars.outcome: "In September 1364, Thado Minbya seized Pinya, and claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya"; Ava was founded in 1365.

certainty.note: No surveyed or treaty border; Sagaing "claimed all the way to the border of Manipur" but its effective control "may have been no more than half today's Sagaing Region", and the only governor-level ruler named in its districts is at Tagaung.
